articles.description: French President Emmanuel Macron has condemned a deadly shooting in the Paris suburbs as a “racist terrorist attack” after one person was killed and five others were injured. The gunman allegedly opened fire from a car in Trappes and nearby La Verrière, appearing to target people of migrant origin. A 12-year-old girl is among those seriously injured. Visiting the scene, Macron said people had been targeted because of their skin colour or religion and called the incident a turning point for France. The National Anti-Terrorist Prosecutor's Office is investigating the attack, although the suspect's exact motive remains unclear.

articles.title: Delhi Metro Poster Row: Police File FIR After Anti-Government Messages Found on Airport Line | N18
articles.description: A political controversy has emerged after two anti-government posters were found pasted inside a train on Delhi Metro’s Airport Express Line. The Delhi Police has registered an FIR against unidentified persons and launched an investigation to establish who was behind the posters and the online group promoted through a QR code. The posters reportedly questioned the government’s performance and listed nine claims about changes in the country over recent years. They also included a QR code inviting passengers to join an online group, prompting investigators to examine the digital trail and identify those responsible. The case has been registered under the Delhi Prevention of Defacement of Public Property Act and the Metro Railways Act. The Delhi Police Special Cell has joined the probe, with investigators looking into who pasted the material inside the train and who administers the online group linked to the QR code. n18oc_breakingnews

NATO’s Patriot Problem: Poland Says No More Missiles For Ukraine As US Rebuilds Iran War Stocks
articles.description: Poland says it cannot provide Ukraine with additional Patriot interceptors as NATO faces growing pressure on its air-defence ammunition stocks. Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski said the shortage worsened following attacks on Iran, with American demand increasing as Washington seeks to replenish its own inventories. Sikorski warned that Russia is producing more missiles than NATO currently has interceptors available to neutralise them, calling the imbalance “a real problem.” Ukraine is seeking 300 additional Patriot interceptors as Russian missile attacks intensify. But Warsaw says Poland is no longer among the NATO members capable of contributing missiles from existing stocks and can only urge other allies to help. The Netherlands has similarly said it exhausted its ability to provide additional Patriots from its own inventory. Years of transfers to Ukraine, increased American requirements following the Iran conflict and slow production of sophisticated interceptors are now colliding — leaving Kyiv’s supporters facing a basic problem: willingness to supply Ukraine does not necessarily mean missiles remain available to give.

articles.description: Iran has a chilling message for American voters ahead of the US midterm elections. Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf has warned Washington that a war with Iran could bring devastating consequences, using a dark “10 poisonous pills” metaphor inspired by the Hollywood film The Matrix. In a post on X, Ghalibaf declared, “Ten pills, all bad. No red, no blue. All soot,” urging US decision-makers to “break the manufactured matrix” and leave. His message comes amid mounting concerns over the economic fallout of the US-Iran war and its impact on ordinary Americans.
